nodes.label: Book Management
nodes.rationale: Supports CRUD, search by name/author, soft delete, and reactivation for books.

nodes.label: Borrow Workflow
nodes.rationale: Models actual library workflows: validate member, validate books, enforce business rules (active member, active book, available copies, max borrow limit, duplicate prevention), create borrow transaction, create borrow records, decrease available copies.

nodes.label: Member Management
nodes.rationale: Supports CRUD plus soft delete and reactivation for members.

nodes.label: Return Workflow
nodes.rationale: Handles returning one or multiple books, automatic fine calculation, updating available copies, calculating total fine, and returning a summary response.

nodes.label: POST /api/auth/register
nodes.rationale: Public signup restricted to MEMBER role only.

nodes.label: Login Response DTO
nodes.rationale: Login response includes accessToken (JWT), tokenType (Bearer), userId, email, role, and expiresIn (seconds). Rationale: tokenType allows frontend to construct Authorization header; userId/email let frontend display user info without decoding JWT; role enables conditional UI rendering; expiresIn helps frontend schedule token refresh.

nodes.label: DTO Pattern
nodes.rationale: DTOs are used to decouple API surface from internal domain entities.

nodes.label: Soft Delete Pattern
nodes.rationale: Both members and books use soft delete with reactivation, preserving referential integrity and audit history.

nodes.label: User Deactivation Security Bug
nodes.rationale: UserPrincipal.isEnabled() is hardcoded to return true and refreshAccessToken never checks user.getIsActive(). A deactivated user can still log in and keep minting access tokens for the full 7-day refresh token lifetime. Fix: add active check at authentication and in refreshAccessToken, throw UserDeactivatedException if inactive.

nodes.label: Spring Boot Actuator Endpoints (perf profile)
nodes.rationale: health and metrics actuator endpoints exposed in perf profile only, enabling external monitoring/assertions during performance test runs without exposing endpoints in production config.

nodes.label: HikariCP Connection Pool (perf profile)
nodes.rationale: Named pool 'library-pool' with maximum-pool-size=10 added in perf profile to cap concurrency and measure throughput under bounded conditions.

nodes.label: JPA/Hibernate Configuration (perf profile)
nodes.rationale: show-sql=true and generate_statistics=true enabled in perf profile to observe query counts and SQL activity during performance tests.

nodes.label: Autocommit/Transaction Management Pattern
nodes.rationale: Both profiles disable JDBC autocommit at the Hikari level and set provider_disables_autocommit=true so Hibernate knows it must manage commits explicitly. This pattern prevents double-commit overhead and ensures @Transactional boundaries are the sole commit points.

nodes.label: Spring 'perf' Test Profile
nodes.rationale: A dedicated Spring profile for performance testing that augments (not replaces) the main config with: explicit pool sizing, SQL/statistics logging, longer JWT token lifetime to avoid mid-test refresh, and exposed actuator endpoints for metric scraping.

nodes.label: JWT Configuration (main)
nodes.rationale: Access token expiration is set to 60s (1 min) for main profile — shortened from the commented-out 900s (15 min) value, likely for development/testing convenience. Refresh token is 7 days. Provider_disables_autocommit=true pairs with hikari auto-commit=false to delegate transaction management to Hibernate/Spring, preventing double-commit issues.

nodes.label: JWT Configuration (perf profile)
nodes.rationale: Access token expiration raised to 300s (5 min) in perf profile vs 60s in main, avoiding token-refresh churn during longer-running performance test runs. Same shared secret ensures tokens issued in tests are valid throughout.
